subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Which public host-local media root policy should OpenClaw support for Telegram outbound media: shared `tools.fs.roots`, a narrower media-only `mediaLocalRoots` surface, or no persistent root expansion?
rationale: The requested fix changes what host-local files can be read and uploaded by message delivery, and repository policy treats new config/default surfaces plus filesystem boundaries as maintainer/security decisions.

options.title: Use shared filesystem roots
options.body: Adopt a single security-reviewed `tools.fs.roots`-style contract for filesystem tools and outbound media so OpenClaw does not grow competing allowlists.

options.title: Add media-only roots
options.body: Add a narrower media-root config if maintainers want outbound media reads separated from read/write/edit filesystem policy, with explicit docs and tests for the split boundary.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Do not add persistent host-root expansion and continue relying on managed roots, concrete-source widening, copies, symlinks, or staged media.

recommendation.title: Use shared filesystem roots
recommendation.body: Adopt a single security-reviewed `tools.fs.roots`-style contract for filesystem tools and outbound media so OpenClaw does not grow competing allowlists.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the local-root policy and filesystem access gating history in the current implementation.
